rv.q: Nevertheless, much can be forgiven in a musical that so firmly has it heart in the right place, and that’s definitely Sweetee.
While the show is a cheerfully optimistic piece that encourages audiences to dream big, with the right amount of work, it has the potential to do the same.
Unfortunately, Sweetee seems rather thin considering the possibilities inherent in the story line. The score is pleasant but innocuous and unmemorable, always a deal breaker in a musical.
Sweetee is a unified, dynamic production that is well-acted, lyrically sung, precisely directed/choreographed (Patricia Birch), staged and set with minimalistic brilliance.
Sweetie may not yet be a total confection, but she's a gal worth keeping an eye on.
Overall, I enjoyed the show. The actors are lively, engaging and charismatic... But in the end I wanted a stronger emotional attachment to the characters and their lives.
I take my hat off to these performers who were given material that is untuneful, lyrically a bore with missed accents and a book that seems more community theatre than off Broadway.
